statement: An infinite concatenation of expanding residual blocks with no contracting itinerary is not a strictly smaller class than MinimalNonTerm. A CE never realizes an exponent-gap itinerary, and expanding concatenations stay expanding, so the leftover is the unbounded CE branch already isolated by the non-escape spine. Window n < 801: 87/87 persistent residual blocks expand; 83 later residuals stay above the original start while contracting versus their own x, which is not PE. This is not a finite PE-run bound and not a halt theorem.

If u and v are expanding itineraries (2^{|u|} < 3^{#O(u)} and 2^{|v|} < 3^{#O(v)}), then u ++ v is expanding: 2^{|u|+|v|} = 2^{|u|} 2^{|v|} < 3^{#O(u)} 3^{#O(v)}. A concatenation of expanding residual blocks is never an exponent-gap certificate. This is not a finite PE-run bound and not a halt theorem.

If MinimalNonTerm n and n follows w, then w is not an exponent-gap itinerary, and every prefix of w is noncontracting. Contrapositive of power_bound_contracts plus minimal_nonterm_no_descent. Concatenating expanding residual blocks therefore cannot create an exponent certificate on a CE. This is not a proof that escape is impossible and not a halt theorem.
